Pu,

W has an overall charge of +1.6  10–19

How many protons, neutrons and electrons are in W?

hints: Look at the $^{239}_{94}\text{Pu}$ notation and recall which number gives protons and which gives total nucleons.
Use $\text{neutrons} = \text{nucleon number} - \text{proton number}$ with 239 and 94 to fix the nucleus, which is unchanged when an ion forms.
Compare the ion charge $+1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ with the elementary charge $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$ to decide how many electrons were removed from the neutral 94-electron atom.
walkthrough: The notation $^{239}_{94}\text{Pu}$ gives proton number $Z = 94$ and nucleon number $A = 239$. Ion formation only changes electrons, so protons are unchanged.
A neutral Pu atom has equal protons and electrons, so it starts with 94 electrons.
The ion charge is $+1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$, which equals $+1e$ since $e = 1.6 \times 10^{-19} \text{ C}$. A $+1e$ charge means one electron has been removed.
Electrons in W are therefore $94 - 1 = 93$. So W has 94 protons, 145 neutrons and 93 electrons. This is option A.

A.explanation: Protons stay at 94, neutrons are $239-94=145$, and one electron lost leaves $94-1=93$ electrons.

B.explanation: 95 electrons would mean one extra electron gained, giving a $1e$ negative ion, not a positive charge.

C.explanation: It swaps the meanings of 239 and 94, but 94 is the proton number and 239 is the nucleon number.

D.explanation: It treats 239 as protons and 94 as neutrons, which reverses the $^{A}_{Z}X$ notation.
